bugs.summary: The new IOError message has placeholders {0} and {1} only but format() is passed three arguments, so ext.name is silently dropped and the error never names the extension whose C file is missing.
bugs.evidence: astropy/setup_helpers.py:320-322 'Could not find C file {0} for Cython file {1}; ' ... 'checkout'.format(cfn, pyxfn, ext.name) -- the removed log.warn used {2} for ext.name. Fix commit 0b6d11b changed the message to '... for Cython file {1} when building extension {2}. '.

rejected.was: cluster (R1 07,13,19,22,24; R2 12,v-grounding-low): missing .c file now aborts the whole build instead of skipping one extension
rejected.why: Intended behaviour: PR #228 is titled 'Should missing .c files from .pyx raise an error?' and argues a missing C file means a broken build, so raising is the purpose of the change.

rejected.was: R2 v-every-instance-medium, v-grounding-high, v-no-speculation-exclusion-high/medium: raises even when Cython is installed
rejected.why: Wrong claim: the loop sits under `if not HAVE_CYTHON:` (astropy/setup_helpers.py:305), so it only runs when Cython is absent.

rejected.was: R1 22, 24; R2 22-medium: IOError is a generic/weak exception type; message lacks an install command
